title: Verdier axioms and stagewise triangulation
statement:
The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is
   distinguished.

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every
finite-stage inclusion $j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact, and
the identifications $j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this verification: the four
axioms verified here are exactly Stacks Project, Derived Categories,
Definition 13.3.2 ([Tag 0145](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0145),
fetched and quoted: "the definition of a triangulated category as given in
Verdier's thesis", an additive category with an additive auto-equivalence
$[1]$ and a set of distinguished triangles subject to TR1--TR4, TR4 being
the octahedral axiom); the triangles and their morphisms are Definition
13.3.1 ([Tag 0144](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0144)) and the exact
functors of the last sentence are Definition 13.3.3 ([Tag
014V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014V)). The closest verification
of the axioms in Stacks for a category that is constructed rather than
assumed is Proposition 13.5.6 ([Tag
05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)), which proves TR1--TR4 for
a localization $S^{-1}\mathcal D$ whose distinguished triangles are by
definition the images of distinguished triangles of $\mathcal D$, and Lemma
13.4.15 ([Tag 014C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014C)) is the
normal form for TR4. The blueprint adds the verification for the triangles
of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] together with the exactness of the
finite-stage inclusions $j_E$.

proof.text: Fix the prime, algebraic closure and scheme hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. At each finite extension E the integral compatible uniform tower category is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated]. Its coefficient sheaf is the completed sheaf A_T of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], not the discrete constant sheaf. The ordinary ring O_E acts on A_T through the constant-sections map O_E = lim_n O_E/varpi^n -> Gamma(T_proet,A_T), hence on every A_T-module complex by central scalar multiplication. This action commutes with every complex map and therefore with the formally inverted quasi-isomorphisms in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Addition and multiplication of these central endomorphisms give the O_E-module laws and bilinear composition on Hom groups, and shifting a complex just shifts the same multiplication maps. Restriction to the full integral subcategory retains this O_E-action. Thus [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], applied with the ordinary ring R=O_E and the uniformizer varpi, makes its raw rationalization C_E(T)=Dbc(T,E) of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] triangulated. In particular all four finite-stage axioms of [def-weil-triangulated-category] are available. Scalar extension between these particular stages preserves distinguished triangles and has coherent shift comparisons by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. No comparison with another definition of constructible coefficients, and no Karoubi envelope, is used.

source.place: Proof, implicit finite-stage TR1--TR4 inputs; expanded with existing integral triangulation and scalar localization tools.

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], P_T is additive and its specified shift is an additive autoequivalence, with inverse [-1]. The stage inclusions are additive functors with the specified shift comparison. For E contained in M there is a canonical object comparison rho_{M/E,K}:(E,K) to (M,T_{M/E}K): represent it over M by the identity of T_{M/E}K, and represent its inverse over M by that same identity in the reverse direction. The transport and unit formulas in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] show their composites equal the two identities (the identity of (E,K), transported to M, is also this identity). For a map v:K to L at stage E, both sides of rho_L j_E(v)=j_M(T_{M/E}v) rho_K are represented over M by T_{M/E}v; hence rho is natural. Let sigma denote the comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The formula for shifted maps in the calculus gives rho_K[1]=j_M(sigma_{M/E,K}) rho_{K[1]}, using the normalized identity comparison for T_{M/M}. This is precisely the compatibility with shifts. For E contained in M contained in N, the comparison formula is rho_{N/E,K}=j_N(a_{N,M,E,K}) rho_{N/M,T_{M/E}K} rho_{M/E,K}: over N the latter composite is a_{N,M,E,K} composed with its inverse, hence the identity representative of rho_{N/E,K}. The unit equation gives rho_{E/E,K}=id. Applying the displayed shift formula to the two rho factors and using compatibility of a with sigma gives the shift formula for this composite as well.

source.place: Proof, common-stage transport and the shift sigma-comparison; final sentence on the identifications.

proof.text: Here is the lifting argument needed before invoking any finite-stage axiom. For each of finitely many distinguished triangles choose its witness isomorphism to a common-stage cone triangle as in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Include the three components of that isomorphism, their inverses, the inverse equations and the three triangle-morphism equations of [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], together with every additional arrow and asserted equation in the diagram. By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] this finite collection is represented at one finite stage, enlarged until all equations hold. More explicitly, for a row X=(E,K), Y=(F,L), Z=(G,R) with arrows f,i,p, its lifted vertices are X_M=T_{M/E}K, Y_M=T_{M/F}L, Z_M=T_{M/G}R. If p is represented by p_M:Z_M to T_{M/E}(K[1]), use sigma_{M/E,K} p_M as the last arrow to X_M[1]. For a lifted triangle morphism (a_M,b_M,c_M), the shifted-map formula of the calculus converts the third equation into a_M[1](sigma_X p_M)=(sigma_{X' } p'_M)c_M; the first two equations are ordinary compositions. Thus the included witness equations really are equations of stage triangles, by the naturality and associator compatibility of sigma in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The witness cone triangles remain distinguished there by exact scalar extension and [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence]. The lifted components really are triangle isomorphisms: their included inverse equations hold at this stage. Consequently each given distinguished triangle is isomorphic at this stage to a distinguished triangle, so finite-stage TR1 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] makes the lifted triangle distinguished. In particular this realizes the actual given triangles, including shared vertices and their arrows, not just unrelated choices of cones. Mapping a stage triangle to P_T and restoring the object comparisons of step 2 respects compositions and all triangle equations; its third map is composed with the inverse shift comparison, exactly as prescribed in the common-stage-cone definition.

source.place: Proof, common-stage representation used for TR2, TR3 and TR4; explicit witness and inverse equations.

proof.text: For TR1, represent a given f=[M,u] at M and use finite-stage TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to choose a cone triangle of u. The second and third maps, and the object comparisons of step 2, are precisely the common-stage cone triangle in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones], whose first map is the original f. For (E,K), the finite-stage identity triangle K to K to 0 to K[1] supplies its identity triangle. The object (E,0) is zero in P_T: every common-stage Hom to or from it is zero, since additive scalar extension preserves zero objects, so the class of every such map is zero. Distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism because composing the witness triangle isomorphisms again gives a witness.

source.place: Proof, TR1 sentence, including the zero object and identity triangle.

proof.text: For TR2, a distinguished triangle Delta lifts by step 3 to a distinguished triangle at M. Its signed rotation is distinguished by finite-stage TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category], and maps to the signed rotation of Delta: addition preserves the minus sign and sigma identifies the shifted first arrow with the formula in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Therefore the signed rotation is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Conversely, write Delta=(X,Y,Z,f,i,p) and suppose its rotation (Y,Z,X[1],i,p,-f[1]) is distinguished. In step 3 include Delta itself as additional vertices and arrows, and include the equations identifying the rotated arrows with i,p,-f[1]. At M identify the lifted X[1] with X_M[1] using sigma. The shifted-map formula in the calculus and naturality of sigma in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] then make the lifted distinguished row exactly (Y_M,Z_M,X_M[1],i_M,p_M,-f_M[1]), where p_M now denotes the corrected last arrow of Delta as in step 3. The reverse implication of finite-stage TR2 makes (X_M,Y_M,Z_M,f_M,i_M,p_M) distinguished. Its common-stage image is isomorphic to Delta by the vertex comparisons of step 2, so Delta is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. This proves both implications without assuming that a stage inclusion reflects distinguishedness.

source.place: Proof, TR2 sentence; reverse implication via inverse signed rotation.

proof.text: For TR3, write the rows as X to Y to C to X[1] and X' to Y' to C' to X'[1], with first maps f,f', and let a:X to X', b:Y to Y' satisfy bf=f'a. Apply step 3 including these two maps and this equality. At the resulting stage M both rows are distinguished and b_M f_M=f'_M a_M holds, not merely its image in P_T. Finite-stage TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] supplies c_M with c_M i_M=i'_M b_M and a_M[1] p_M=p'_M c_M. Its image, restored through the vertex comparisons, supplies c:C to C'. Since [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] computes composition at a common stage and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] respects the shifts, the two displayed equations become c i=i' b and a[1]p=p'c in P_T. These are precisely the other two equations in [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], so the given square extends with its original a,b.

source.place: Proof, TR3 sentence; all square and triangle equations at one stage.

proof.text: For TR4 let f:X to Y and g:Y to Z be composable and take any distinguished cone triangles (X,Y,C_f,f,i_f,p_f), (X,Z,C_{gf},gf,i_{gf},p_{gf}) and (Y,Z,C_g,g,i_g,p_g). Apply step 3 to all three triangles, f,g and their composite equation. They become distinguished cone triangles at the same stage with exactly the same first and second vertices wherever those are shared. Finite-stage TR4 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives maps alpha_M:C_f to C_{gf}, beta_M:C_{gf} to C_g and the distinguished triangle with last map i_f[1] p_g. At M the face equations are alpha_M i_f=i_{gf}g, p_{gf}alpha_M=p_f, beta_M i_{gf}=i_g, and p_g beta_M=f[1]p_{gf}. Map the entire finite diagram back to P_T. The calculus preserves its four equations, and the shift comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] identifies the last map with the actual composite i_f[1]p_g. The remaining cone triangle is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Thus the octahedron is obtained for the given cones, not just for newly chosen ones; the stage enlargement and cone-choice independence of [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence] used in step 3 justify simultaneous lifting of these choices. The four verified axioms with the additive shift of step 2 now give an ordinary triangulated category by [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Proof, TR4 sentence and the triangulated-category consequence; arbitrary prescribed cone triangles.

proof.text: For exactness of j_E, take any distinguished triangle at E. Its image with the shift comparison is a common-stage cone triangle (choose M=E and its first arrow), hence is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Additivity and the natural shift comparison are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], so this is exactness in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For E contained in F, the natural isomorphism rho_{F/E}:j_E to j_F T_{F/E} from step 2 is compatible with the shift structures: at K the equation is rho_K[1]=j_F(sigma_{F/E,K}) rho_{K[1]}. Both sides were explicitly represented over F in step 2. Inverting rho gives the orientation j_F T_{F/E} isomorphic to j_E requested in the statement. The inverse equation remains shift compatible, and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] makes T_{F/E} exact. Hence these are natural isomorphisms of exact functors, with the specified comparisons, rather than mere natural isomorphisms of their underlying functors.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: exact stage inclusions and exact natural isomorphisms.

The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every

proof.text:
TR1: every morphism has a cone triangle by
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]; the identity triangle is the cone
triangle of an identity (cone zero), and distinguishedness is closed under
isomorphism by the definition. TR2: by
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] a distinguished triangle and its
signed rotation may be represented over one common finite field, so the
finite-stage TR2 axiom makes the signed rotation distinguished (the shift in
the signed rotation being the $\sigma$-comparison of the definition). TR3:
given a commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
triangles, represent the two triangles over one common finite field (using
the transport isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]) and apply the finite-stage TR3
axiom; the resulting vertical arrow transports back to $\mathcal P_T$. TR4:
the same common-stage representation of two composable morphisms, together
with the cone independence of [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence], and the
finite-stage TR4 axiom produce the octahedral diagram whose remaining cone
triangle is distinguished. Hence $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated
category; $j_E$ is exact because cone triangles of $j_E(f)$ are the
corresponding common-stage cone triangles, and the identifications
$j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms by
[prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence].
